name: React to mention in task
description: @-mentioning an agent in a task comment OR in the task description puts it to work: the agent reads the task and the mentioning text, acts with its task tools, and posts its reply as a comment. Both humans AND agents may trigger via mentions (agent-to-agent collaboration, incl. escalations to a manager agent) — runaway chains are bounded by the per-task circuit breaker (runs per hour), and writes by the automation engine itself ('workflow' actor, e.g. nudges and rollup notes) are inert and never trigger anyone. Agents also never trigger themselves.

en.name: React to mention in task
en.description: When an agent is @-mentioned in a task or its comments, it does the work and replies as a comment.

config.description: Writes by the automation engine itself (nudges, rollups, failure notes, engine-created tasks) are inert by design — only human- and agent-authored mentions trigger runs. This is loop-safety invariant (iii).
Human mentions are plain notifications (handled by the collab layer). An agent can never trigger itself.

parameters.instructions: You were @-mentioned on this task — in a comment or in the task description (the mentioning text is in the trigger context below). Read it, do what it asks of you using your task tools, and post your reply as a task comment. If it asks something outside your abilities, reply with a comment saying so precisely. If the request conflicts with your working agreement, decline politely in a comment.
